What is the essential teaching in '30. What to watch'?

In '30. What to watch', the teaching opens with this observation: *"What to watch]
Luang Taa Naen ordained well after middle age."* The central invitation is to turn one's investigation inward — to verify the Dhamma not as a set of beliefs, but as directly observable reality in one's own body, speech, and mind. As the text teaches, the Dhamma is *akāliko* — ever-present — and *opanayiko* — leading inward — available to be known (*paccattaṁ*) by each practitioner for themselves. There is no need to search elsewhere; the truth is already here.

This section teaches: *"Luang Taa Naen ordained well after middle age. Illiterate and unable to speak a word of Central Thai, he had his strong point in that he was well-intentioned, tractable, and diligent in his duties, to the point where you couldn’t fault him. When he saw other monks taking their leave to go wandering or to study with other ajaans, he decided that he ..."* The core instruction is to turn investigation inward (*opanayiko*) toward what is already present in body, speech, and mind — not to seek the Dhamma outside or in future states. Whatever theme this section addresses, the method is the same: sustained, patient, non-grasping awareness that allows the truth to reveal itself. As Ajahn Mun taught: when the mind sees clearly, there is no longer any need to go looking.
